title: Newton's Inequality: Normalized (Cleared-Denominator) Inductive Proof
description: Completes the inductive proof of Newton's inequality in cleared-denominator form: C(n,k-1)·C(n,k+1)·e_k² ≥ C(n,k)²·e_{k-1}·e_{k+1} for nonneg reals. Also proves ultra-log-concavity of binomial coefficients (C(n,k)⁴ ≥ C(n,k-1)²·C(n,k+1)²) and the unnormalized Newton inequality (e_k² ≥ e_{k-1}·e_{k+1}). The k=1 and boundary k=n cases both reduce to a quadratic-nonneg argument via the key identity 2·C(n+1,k) = n·(n+1) from Pascal's rule.

meta.author: Formalized in Lean 4
originalContributions: Ultra-log-concavity of binomial coefficients: C(n,k)⁴ ≥ C(n,k-1)²·C(n,k+1)²
Unnormalized Newton inequality: e_k² ≥ e_{k-1}·e_{k+1} for nonneg reals
Key identity: 2·C(n+1,p+1) = n·(n+1) via Pascal's rule for boundary case
Quadratic-nonneg reduction: both k=1 and k=n cases via linear_combination ring identity
meta.proofStrategy: Induction on list length. Two boundary cases: k=1 (quadratic in new element x with discriminant from 2·C(n,2)=n·(n-1)) and k=n (quadratic via 2·C(n+1,n-1)=n·(n+1)). Interior cases: esymm_cross_condition plus newton_cleared_denom_inductive_step from AmgmInequalityOQ02OQ02.
